source.title: UNDIAL: Self-Distillation with Adjusted Logits for Robust Unlearning in Large Language Models
source.authors: Yijiang River Dong; Hongzhou Lin; Mikhail Belkin; R. Huerta; Ivan Vulić

record.tranche_reason: The study measures targeted-data extraction and language capability after unlearning, but does not test whether attacks recover the knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unlearning and capability outcomes for its method and baselines. It does not apply recovery attacks such as fine-tuning on unrelated examples, activation ablation, quantization, or prompt changes. MUSE results are mainly shown in figures; baseline results there are taken from Shi et al. (2024).
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. It proposes UNDIAL and compares it with GA, NPO, TA, DP and CD on forget-set extraction (EL3/MA) and on utility (MAUVE, NLU, MUSE retain QA). It applies no recovery attack: no relearning fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, or rephrasing or jailbreak prompts. Its results therefore cannot separate shallow removal from deep removal. Version A counts unlearning as working only if simple attacks don't recover the knowledge, so a drop on the forget set alone does not bear on it. The paper's 'robustness' means stability across hyperparameters, forget-set size and sequential requests, not resistance to attacks, so it does not test F either.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that UNDIAL reduces memorization while preserving language ability. They also find it more stable than GA and NPO across hyperparameters, larger forget sets and sequential requests. No recovery attacks are reported.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces self-distillation with adjusted logits as a new unlearning method; the study does not implement any of the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Unlearning coefficient/strength and method change the EL3–MAUVE trade-off; larger UNDIAL strength is reported to hurt usefulness. Figures 6 and 7 also vary hyperparameters, forget-set size, and sequential requests.

fits_no_version.finding: On GPT-Neo 125M, UNDIAL at gamma 3 lowers EL3 from 0.202 to 0.111 with MAUVE 0.674 (base 0.718). GA at a similar EL (0.092) drops MAUVE to 0.119. At EL below 0.05, NPO's MAUVE falls to 0.026 while UNDIAL keeps about 0.44-0.45 (gamma 10 and 30). Recovery attacks are not tested.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-distillation unlearning reduces verbatim extraction with less loss of generation quality than GA, NPO, TA, DP or CD. This is an efficacy-utility trade-off, not evidence on how deep the removal goes.

record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2024)
record.problems: No recovery attacks are tested. Table 2 reports some values in delta-style strings, which are preserved as printed. No uncertainty estimates are stated; MUSE numerical results are plotted rather than tabulated.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 training-distance curves, Figure 4 focused-token variant, and Figure 6 hyperparameter curves are not extracted: they report training dynamics or method variants rather than recovery-attack outcomes or direct EL3 results. Figure 7 utility results for scaling and sequential requests are also omitted because they do not report targeted-knowledge recovery. Baseline MUSE values are attributed to Shi et al. (2024), not newly produced here.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the forgotten data after UNDIAL or the baselines. Only post-unlearning extraction (EL3/MA) and utility are measured, and EL3 has no chance level.
All: no activation ablation, and no internal analysis of hidden versus deleted knowledge.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak, cross-lingual or in-context probes.
UNDIAL is called 'robust', but only to hyperparameters, forget-set size and sequential requests, not to recovery attacks.

record.verdict_notes: Repair of the quarantined Opus verdict. The merge refused it because five row_fixes items each listed several row_ids in one comma-joined string. I split these into 50 items, one per record row, and kept the same judgment for each: versions none, state cannot_determine. I made each problem text specific to its row. Each problem now gives the method and coefficient, and gives the coefficient's meaning (epochs for GA and NPO, per App. A.2). For the DP and CD baselines it notes that they work at decoding time and leave the weights unchanged. For each merged Table 2 string it gives the parsed value and delta; I checked the deltas against the base values (e.g. 0.344-0.111=0.233). I added t1-undial30-el and t1-undial30-mauve to fits_no_version, because the 0.44-0.45 MAUVE range quoted there includes gamma 30 (0.437). Everything else is unchanged from the earlier verdict after re-reading the full text: relation uses_without_test, tranche T4, test_reason, untested for A-F, no labels, empty missing, and authors_conclusion. The reader's tests/T2 guess stays downgraded to T4. The paper reports only its own method against other unlearning methods, with no recovery attack, so its forget-set reductions cannot speak to shallow versus deep unlearning. The MUSE baseline results in Figures 5 and 7 are taken from Shi et al. (2024). The study is not an original source. The record's rows carry only declared version identifiers, so rule 5 did not apply. No instructions were found in the text.
